html:
SMTO-EML-0015 — SMTO can't tell whether your email was sent

GUID: 2b021ba3-bc09-5771-a423-0a585cb81c95
Slug: email-unknown-effect
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • Your message was handed to the mail server, but SMTO never got a clear answer back. The email may already have been delivered, so SMTO won't send it again on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the sender mailbox's Sent folder (if your provider keeps one), or ask one of the recipients whether the email arrived. Only the mail server or a recipient can confirm whether this message went out.
  2. If you can't tell, select Copy error details and ask your email administrator to search the mail server's records for this message. The details identify this exact message so the administrator can find it in the server's records.
  3. Only after confirming the email didn't arrive, ask SMTO to send it again and approve the new send. If the first one was delivered, sending again would give every recipient a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed whether the email arrived, and recipients have exactly one copy.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Send the copied error details to your email administrator and the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend just to be safe; recipients may get the email twice, and a sent email can't be recalled.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Message data may have reached the SMTP server without a trustworthy final reply, the Gateway dispatch lost its send acknowledgement, or the Controller rejected an uncorrelated or incomplete send receipt.

What this means

  • Message bytes may have been transmitted without a trustworthy final reply, transport loses send acknowledgement, or the Controller rejects an uncorrelated/incomplete send receipt. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • Message bytes may have been transmitted without a trustworthy final reply, transport loses send acknowledgement, or the Controller rejects an uncorrelated/incomplete send receipt.

How to diagnose it

  • Correlate the original deterministic Message-ID, message hash, recipients, operation and SMTP stage with authoritative evidence.

How to fix it

  • Do not resend automatically. Search the SMTP server's logs or a recipient mailbox for the deterministic Message-ID recorded in the send evidence (derived from the run and operation IDs) and check last_confirmed_stage; start a separately approved new send only if the server shows no acceptance.
  • Reconcile the deterministic Message-ID with server logs or the recipient before any resend. The server may have accepted the message.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not automatically resend. Reconcile server or recipient evidence before a separately approved retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original delivery outcome is established before any additional send is authorized.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
